source_text.GH#2325: ISS-1035 (legacy title) / Q-1017: a HUMAN_TASK escalation timer always CANCELS the task; there is no non-cancelling reminder, so long-running tasks (vortex 8D corrective action) can only carry an E6 waiver. ACs (binding, from gh issue view 2325 --comments): (1) a REQ-xxx in docs/requirements.yaml, validated by REQ-VALIDATOR, defining the non-cancelling reminder (attributes, repeat rule, what it does, audit event, validator checks); (2) design states interaction with escalation timers and task completion/cancellation (reminder timers cancelled when the task completes or is cancelled); (3) after implementation the vortex corrective-action-8d waiver is replaced by a reminder (separate task) and the definition-level test accepts a reminder as an alternative to a waiver; (4) SECURITY-REVIEWER n/a unless notifications cross tenants.

task.description: WF-03 step 1 diagnosis for GH #2325 (tvolodi-org/letflow; legacy title ISS-1035, old queue Q-1017). Diagnosis only: no lib/ or test/ edits, no commits, no push/PR/GitHub writes, no queue calls. This is a capability gap (feature request routed through WF-03), not a regression: the binding AC1 requires a validated requirement first, so the downstream route is WF-01 (REQ-ANALYST -> REQ-VALIDATOR) before CODE-DESIGNER. Produce with file:line evidence: (1) the escalation/timer types that exist today, how escalation is armed/fired/cancelled, the CHK-21 validator check and the E6 waiver mechanism; (2) the notification/inbox/audit facilities a reminder could reuse and what does not exist; (3) shipped definitions using escalation timers or a waiver and the vortex corrective-action-8d waiver location; (4) backward compatibility of an opt-in reminder attribute set, whether a migration is needed, and the interaction with the merged GH #2359 change; (5) a proposed scope split (requirement content, minimal implementation slice, separate vortex follow-up) with blast radius and tenant-data-path relevance.
acceptance_criteria: Every factual claim cites file:line read from the branch (cut from origin/main incl. 05a0dfeb1, GH #2359 fix); nothing is asserted from the issue prose alone.
States plainly which notification/inbox facilities do NOT exist so the requirement does not assume them.
States whether a DB migration is needed, quoting the timers migration and the Timer schema guard.
States the GH #2359 cancel-before-arm ordering constraint a reminder must respect and names gh2359_gateway_reentry_task_row_test.exs as a must-stay-green test.

Gives a requirement scope (attributes, repeat rule, fire behaviour, audit event, validator checks, cancellation points) and an implementation slice with per-module blast radius, plus the separate vortex waiver-replacement follow-up.
No implementation written; handoff file uses exactly the step-01 schema of WF03-GH2359-GATEWAYBACK-20261014.

result.summary:
DIAGNOSIS (code-read, file:line evidence; no test run was needed: the gap is a missing feature, and the escalation-cancels behaviour is already pinned by test/letflow/engine/human_task_escalation_test.exs and vortex_escalation_timer_test.exs). Registry lookup (Step 0.5): no docs/issues entry for ISS-1035 exists (docs/issues/ISS-1017.yaml is an unrelated bilimbaga roster issue); the only prior record is docs/issues/ISS-1002.yaml:52-54,63,65 (waiver accepted pending this gap). Not a recurrence. CLASSIFICATION: capability gap, not a defect; AC1 requires WF-01 (REQ-ANALYST/REQ-VALIDATOR) before CODE-DESIGNER.

(1) TIMER/ESCALATION TODAY. Timer types: lib/letflow/scheduler/timer.ex:48 `@timer_types ["deadline", "reminder", "escalation", "scheduled_transition"]` -- "reminder" is ALREADY an allowed value but nothing produces it; guard is changeset-only `validate_inclusion(:timer_type, @timer_types)` (timer.ex:129). TIMER nodes arm timer_type "deadline" from `duration_iso8601` (engine.ex:777-797, CHK-12). HUMAN_TASK escalation (REQ-396): attributes `escalation_timer_duration` (ISO-8601 string) + `escalation_role` (non-blank string). Arm: Transition.dispatch_human_task/3 emits `{:escalation_timer_armed, token_id, node_id}` only when the duration is a non-empty binary (transition.ex:438-452); Engine.prepare_timer_arms/4 -> resolve_escalation_timer_arm_attrs/4 builds `timer_type: "escalation", fire_at: now + seconds` (engine.ex:713-751, 802-827); build_timer_arms_multi/4 uses step name `{:scheduler_escalation_timer, token_record_id}` (engine.ex:848-857). Fire: Scheduler.do_fire/2 marks fired, appends TIMER_FIRED (scheduler.ex:301-306, 373-393), then routes `"escalation" -> Letflow.Engine.advance_after_escalation_timer_fired`, `_ -> Letflow.Engine.advance_after_timer_fired` (scheduler.ex:311-317), then maybe_rearm_timer (scheduler.ex:323). Escalation semantics: stale guard (token moved off node -> no-op, engine.ex:2979-2983, 3016-3024); transition `{:escalation_timer_fired, ...}` 'Skip conditioned edges entirely -- unconditionally follow the fallback edge' and takes `List.first(default_edges)` (transition.ex:699-718); persist step `:cancel_original_task` sets the pending task row `status: :cancelled` and writes audit `action: "task.cancel"` (engine.ex:3105-3158). Cancellation of escalation timers: on normal completion `Multi.run(:cancel_escalation_timers, ...)` -> TaskActivation.cancel_pending_escalation_timers/6 (engine.ex:4543-4558; task_activation.ex:555-577, scoped `instance_id, token_id, node_id, timer_type == "escalation", status == "pending"`, cancel_reason "task_completed"); on instance completion/cancel ALL pending timers of the instance via cancel_pending_timers/5 (engine.ex:2045-2052 reason "instance_completed"; engine.ex:5768-5774 reason "instance_cancelled"; task_activation.ex:535-545, not type-scoped). Validator CHK-21: graph.ex:1071-1131 (codes :invalid_escalation_timer, :missing_escalation_role, :missing_escalation_timer_duration; pair co-required, duration via valid_iso8601_duration?/1, 'P0D' accepted). Role binding collects `["role", "escalation_role"]` (role_binding.ex:26-41). E6 WAIVER: NOT an engine/validator concept. It exists only as a convention in definition-level tests: `waiver?/1` = description starting `Waiver:` + non-empty reason (test/letflow/scripts/vortex_d_esc_escalation_fixture_test.exs:108-114, same in meridian_...:111-116 and swiftroute_...:99-104), XOR rule `assert pair?(n) != waiver?(n)` (vortex test :179-186), pinned 8D test (vortex test :355-362, asserts `~r/^Waiver: long-running remediation work/` and `refute pair?(n)`). The E6 ruling is BA GH #2281 (cited in the fixture text).

(2) FACILITIES. EXISTS: (a) TIMER_FIRED event, appended for EVERY timer type with payload timer_id/node_id/timer_type/fired_late/scheduled/actual (scheduler.ex:373-393), registered per tenant (tenant_provisioning.ex:1129-1150) -- a reminder fire gets an audit event for free with timer_type "reminder". (b) audit_entries via Audit.append_multi/4 (audit.ex:189), `action` is a free :string (migration 20260830020001 `add :action, :string, null: false`, no check), precedent "task.cancel". (c) the 'inbox' is GET /tasks/inbox = Letflow.Tasks.list_tasks/2 over the `tasks` table (routers/tasks.ex:12, 130-131, 225-260) -- pending task rows only. (d) REQ-441 is status done (requirements.yaml:33303-33306) but it is a login-discovery tenant-list mailer (Letflow.LoginDiscovery.Notifier, behaviour deliver_tenant_list/2; default Noop, lib/letflow/login_discovery/dispatch.ex:44), not a general notification channel. DOES NOT EXIST: no notifications table/module, no per-user/role notification item, no 'reminded'/'last_reminded_at'/due_at column on tasks (task.ex:58-74 fields), no general-purpose email/notification port, no engine producer of recurring timers (repeat_expression set only in scheduler_req188_test.exs:203,246,294). A NEW events.event_type needs a registry row in every tenant or EventStore.append returns {:error, :unknown_event_type} (event_store.ex:158; ISS-0072 note tenant_provisioning.ex:845-852; seeded only at provisioning/replay, :864) -- so reusing TIMER_FIRED (+ an audit_entries row, e.g. action "task.remind") avoids a registry change. A 'notification/inbox item for the named role' therefore needs either a new table (migration + tenant-data path + API + SPA) or must be scoped to audit-only in this slice; the requirement must decide explicitly.

(3) SHIPPED DEFINITIONS. Escalation pairs: test/fixtures/qa/meridian_loan_origination_process_definition.json (15 refs), meridian_regulatory_compliance_review_... (6), swiftroute_incident_... (4), swiftroute_process_definition.json (3), vortex_production_order_release_process_definition.json:16,27,41,53, vortex_supplier_quality_deviation_process_definition.json:25,36; simulation YAML meridian/process_claim_intake.yaml (14), meridian/process_policy_binding.yaml (5), swiftroute/process_route_approval.yaml (2), swiftroute/process_shipment_dispatch.yaml (5), vortex/process_quality_check.yaml:22,29,37,44, vortex/process_work_order.yaml:26,33; UAT scenario uat/scenarios/swiftroute/shipment-ops-timeout-escalation.yaml:13 (uses POST /instances/:id/advance-timer, :67). Nothing in priv/ or scripts/ carries escalation attributes in-file (scripts/seed_vortex_definition.sh seeds from the fixtures). Waivers: exactly ONE in-file -- test/fixtures/qa/vortex_8d_corrective_action_definition.json:16 (node corrective-action-8d, attributes.description 'Waiver: long-running remediation work (engine gap ... Q-1017 / GH #2325 / ISS-1035). BA ruling GH #2281, E6. ...'). Swiftroute shipment dispatch states 'no waivers' (process_shipment_dispatch.yaml:59).

(4) BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY. An opt-in attribute set (e.g. reminder_timer_duration + reminder_role [+ reminder_repeat_interval / reminder_repeat_count]) on HUMAN_TASK is inert for every existing definition: arming keys strictly on a non-empty attribute value (pattern of transition.ex:442-449); CHK-21 reads only escalation_* keys (graph.ex:1093-1094); no shipped definition carries reminder_* keys (grep: only docs/requirements.yaml:34478 comment and ISS-1002 mention it). Stored timer rows unchanged: no timer row with timer_type "reminder" is ever produced today. MIGRATION: NOT needed for the timer itself -- timer_type is plain :string with NO DB check (migration 20260829020001_create_timers.exs:26-29 '`timer_type` is plain :string, NOT Ecto.Enum ... application-layer `validate_inclusion/3` ... is the only guard', column :80; only chk_timers_status :106-109 and chk_timers_recurrence_shape :111-121), and "reminder" is already in @timer_types (timer.ex:48). The recurrence quartet (repeat_expression, repeat_interval_us, repeat_total, fired_count) + Scheduler.maybe_rearm_timer/3 (scheduler.ex:445-486, nominal fire_at anchor) already support repeat. A migration IS needed only if the requirement chooses a new notifications table. HAZARDS a design must close: (h1) TODAY a "reminder" row would take the `_ ->` branch into advance_after_timer_fired (scheduler.ex:315-316) and fail with {:token_not_at_timer, :HUMAN_TASK, node} (transition.ex:679-683) -> retries -> DLQ (scheduler.ex:583-638): a dedicated "reminder" branch is mandatory. (h2) maybe_rearm_timer runs unconditionally after the advance (scheduler.ex:323) -- a stale recurring reminder would re-arm forever unless it is cancelled on completion/escalation and the fire path does not re-arm when stale (series cap via repeat_total helps but is not sufficient). (h3) Scheduler.resolve_advance_target/3 returns {:error, :ambiguous_pending_timers} when >1 pending timer and no timer_id (scheduler.ex:348-360): an instance with a reminder AND an escalation pending makes POST /advance-timer without timer_id ambiguous -- affects only opted-in definitions, but UAT scenarios that rely on it must pass timer_id. (h4) escalation fire cancels the task (engine.ex:3116-3133) but cancels no other timer: the reminder must be cancelled in the same Multi. GH #2359 INTERACTION: complete-task Multi runs `:cancel_escalation_timers` BEFORE the arm steps 'so a same-node re-entry's freshly armed escalation timer is not cancelled' (engine.ex:4543-4558); escalation fire uses TaskActivation.consume_completed_position/3 for re-entry (engine.ex:2985-2996). A reminder cancel must be added in that same pre-arm position (widen the type filter to ["escalation","reminder"] or a sibling step), status-guarded on "pending" and scoped token+node, so a re-entered task gets a FRESH reminder. Must stay green: test/letflow/engine/gh2359_gateway_reentry_task_row_test.exs (T-8 asserts exactly one new pending timer of type "escalation" -- unaffected unless its fixture gains reminder_*), human_task_escalation_test.exs, timer_wiring_test.exs, scheduler_test.exs, scheduler_req188_test.exs, the three *_d_esc_escalation_fixture_test.exs.

(5) PROPOSED SCOPE SPLIT. (A) REQUIREMENT (WF-01, REQ-ANALYST -> REQ-VALIDATOR; next free id after REQ-472): HUMAN_TASK optional `reminder_timer_duration` (ISO-8601, >0) + `reminder_role` (non-blank) co-required; optional `reminder_repeat_interval` (ISO-8601) and `reminder_repeat_count` (int >=1, absent = until task closes or a stated cap); fire = TIMER_FIRED (timer_type "reminder") + audit_entries row (action e.g. "task.remind", resource task id, role) with task row, token, instance state and variables UNCHANGED and no edge followed; decide explicitly whether a role-visible notification item is in scope (needs new table/API/SPA => migration, SECURITY-REVIEWER) or deferred, email deferred until a general notifier exists (REQ-441's notifier is login-discovery only); validator CHK-xx mirroring CHK-21 (pair, durations, repeat fields require the pair, optional warning if reminder >= escalation duration); role_binding.task_roles adds "reminder_role"; cancellation points: task completion (pre-arm, GH #2359 order), escalation fire (same Multi as :cancel_original_task), instance completion/cancel (already covered by cancel_pending_timers/5, untyped). (B) IMPLEMENTATION SLICE (ELIXIR-DEV): transition.ex dispatch_human_task emits {:reminder_timer_armed, ...}; engine.ex prepare_timer_arms/build_timer_arms_multi (unique step name per token) + cancel at engine.ex:4547 + cancel in persist_escalation_timer_fired_advance; task_activation.ex cancel helper widened/sibling; scheduler.ex do_fire `"reminder"` branch -> new Engine.record_reminder_fired (stale check like escalation_timer_stale?/2, audit, no advance) and stale-aware re-arm; graph.ex new check; role_binding.ex key; tests. No migration, no new event type if TIMER_FIRED + audit_entries is accepted. Blast radius: engine timer paths (shared by complete_task, timer fire, escalation fire, create) -- medium; scheduler fire routing -- small; validator -- additive. (C) SEPARATE FOLLOW-UP: replace the waiver at vortex_8d_corrective_action_definition.json:16 with reminder attrs (BA: P14D reminder to role-procurement-manager/role-quality-manager per ISS-1002:63), bump 8D version + seed, extend waiver?/pair? XOR in vortex_d_esc_escalation_fixture_test.exs:179-186,355-362 to accept `reminder?` as the waiver alternative, update ISS-1002 follow-up. TENANT-DATA PATH: timers/audit_entries/tasks are tenant-schema tables written with prefix (timer.ex:10-12; scheduler.ex:166 tenant_id from prefix); audit-only slice adds no route and no cross-tenant read -> INV-1/INV-6 satisfied by existing prefix discipline, SECURITY-REVIEWER n/a per AC4; becomes REQUIRED if a notification table/route or email egress is added (INV-1, INV-2, INV-5, INV-6, INV-8; email adds INV-4/INV-9).
